thread:
incident-bot: P0 alert — Embeddings inference 95th-percentile latency above 2.5s in us-west-2 since 12:15 UTC. Auto-page sent to oncall. Investigating. Escalation: mike (oncall) paged.

mike (oncall): on it. grabbing runbook link now. initial hypothesis: KV cache thrash after a large model swap at 12:10. Will confirm with logs.

kevin (infra): I see increased tail latency on the gpu-pool-a nodes, memory pressure spikes around 12:13 across 3 hosts. Pulling dmesg + nvidia-smi.

mike (oncall): team, please help draft statuspage initial notice. Need short, factual wording and customer impact statement. I'll take the ops technical details.

amy (comms): I'll draft message. Quick Q: legal review needed before publishing phrasing that mentions "no data loss"? @legal (team) can you weigh in? :eyes:

legal (team): please avoid definitive language until we've completed log checks. "No evidence of data exfiltration" is OK with a qualifier. We'll join the call if needed.

mike (oncall): copying what i'm planning to post to status page. please review. (paste below)

```
Status: Investigating
Components: Embeddings API (us-west-2)
Started: 2026-03-15T12:15:00Z
Impact: Customers may experience elevated response times (order seconds) for embeddings requests originating in us-west-2. Requests are succeeding but with degraded latency. We are actively investigating and working on mitigation.
Mitigation: Rolling back a recent model routing change and draining affected hosts. No action required from customers. We'll post updates every ~30 minutes or as significant changes occur.
```

amy (comms): good base. Suggest small tweaks: use "elevated latency" and add a short line about expected ETA to next update. I'll prepare a customer-facing blurb to paste into Support.

support-bot: New incident log created: INC-20260315-33. Support notification draft queued in #support.

olivia (ops): mike, I'm starting rollback on canary nodes now, will monitor token throughput and 95th latency. If rollback doesn't help within 10m we'll failover traffic to us-east-1.

kevin (infra): pushed a quick kernel tweak on two nodes to mitigate memory fragmentation; monitoring metrics.

amy (comms): customer-facing email draft for support to send (feedback welcome):

"We are investigating increased latency for embeddings requests in the us-west-2 region. Requests are processing but may be slower than usual. Our engineers are rolling back a recent change and monitoring performance. We will follow up within 30 minutes with an update."

legal (team): language looks fine with the qualifier. please don't claim a root cause yet.

mike (oncall): updated statuspage block with minor wording. Ready to publish initial notice once legal sign-off. Copying final text:

```
Status: Investigating
Components: Embeddings API — us-west-2
Start time: 2026-03-15T12:15:00Z
Customer impact: Some customers in the us-west-2 region may see elevated latency for embeddings requests. Requests are completing but with slower response times.
What we're doing: Engineers are rolling back a recent routing change and draining affected instances. We will continue to monitor and provide periodic updates. No customer action required.
Next update: ~12:45 UTC or sooner.
```

amy (comms): LGTM from comms side. :thumbsup:

legal (team): okay to publish with the current language. minor nit: change "routing change" to "model routing change". then good.

mike (oncall): done. Publishing now to statuspage and notifying support for customer messages.

support-bot: Statuspage update published: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/embeddings-us-west-2. Support notification sent to #support with draft email.

olivia (ops): rollback appears to be helping. 95th latency has dropped from ~2.9s to ~1.1s on canary nodes. Continuing rollout to rest of the pool.

kevin (infra): metrics confirm improving tail across gpu-pool-a. still watching for memory churn.

amy (comms): planning a follow-up statuspage update with ETA to resolution once we see stable metrics for 10 minutes. I'll draft.

mike (oncall): follow-up update (to be published):

```
Status: Identified / Partial mitigation
Components: Embeddings API — us-west-2
Update: We rolled back a recent model routing change and deployed a kernel fix to affected hosts. Observed 95th-tail latency reduced significantly; traffic is being restored to the pool gradually.
Customer impact: Latency is improving; some customers may still observe slower responses as traffic returns to normal.
Next update: 13:15 UTC or earlier if resolved.
```

amy (comms): posted. Customers are being proactively contacted via queued support emails for customers with high-traffic embedding usage.

support-bot: Customer notifications dispatched to 23 enterprise accounts flagged by usage footprint.

mike (oncall): marking this thread for resolved notice preparation. If metrics remain stable for 15m, we'll publish resolved.

olivia (ops): metrics stable for 18m. no error rate increase, success rate steady.

kevin (infra): memory fragmentation alarms have cleared. no repeated spikes.

amy (comms): final resolved statuspage copy (proposal):

```
Status: Resolved
Components: Embeddings API — us-west-2
Start time: 2026-03-15T12:15:00Z
Resolved: 2026-03-15T13:05:00Z
Summary: A recent model routing change caused elevated tail latency for embeddings requests in the us-west-2 region. Engineers rolled back the change and applied mitigations; performance has returned to normal. No customer data was affected.
What we're doing next: Post-incident review scheduled; we'll follow up with action items and timeline for preventing recurrence.
```

legal (team): "No customer data was affected" — ok as long as logs support that. engineering to confirm.

mike (oncall): confirmed logs show no failed writes or exfiltration. publishing resolved now.

support-bot: Statuspage update published: resolved. Customer notifications: final follow-up queued.

amy (comms): thanks team. I'll own the post-incident status page summary and coordinate the follow-up report.

mike (oncall): closing the incident. Thanks everyone for quick responses. :v:
